title: Combining quiet companion dialogue with survival tension (and our AI-assisted indie workflow) — V.E.T.O.R — A Ruptura new trailer
author: Sufficient-Cause2216
selftext:
In our Brazilian indie project **V.E.T.O.R — A Ruptura** (in development for PC/Windows), we are exploring how to make the player care about the relationship between a weary traveler and his floating companion **VETOR** before danger even appears.

Our new trailer — **"Can you feel fear?" (Você consegue sentir medo?)** — starts with a quiet conversation about fear, loneliness, and finding a reason to keep going in a forgotten city. Then they find an abandoned car that might offer a way out, where making noise comes at a price.

▶ **New Trailer (3m18s, Portuguese audio):** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uilEvPMn4gE

**How AI fits into our development workflow:**
- We use **Codex** as a programming and development partner for our custom game systems (including our mid-encounter dialogue and weak-point analysis mechanics) as well as visual workflow support.
- For cinematic trailer transitions and specific atmospheric video scenes like this narrative teaser, we used **Veo** alongside our project's visual references and voice acting direction.
- One of the biggest design challenges we are iterating on right now is making sure the emotional tone of the cinematic conversations connects naturally with the actual 2.5D exploration and combat encounters.

For those of you using AI tools in your game dev pipeline: how do you balance narrative/cinematic mood pieces with core gameplay showcases? And in a survival scenario like this, would you keep trying to start the car or leave it behind?
